item: forensics.py defined _seconds_between twice: the later one won for the module and main went red
summary: Two pull requests, each green on its own tree, each added a top-level _seconds_between to src/monitoring/forensics.py (a float of seconds for the collect-perf tick; a whole number, None for a reversed order, for the previous session's teardown time). Python keeps the later definition for the whole module, so the tick's time-into-the-pass read 1 instead of 1.5 and tests/test_session_forensics.py failed on main and in every pull request cut from it. The second is renamed _whole_seconds_between at its definition and its one call. tests/test_no_duplicate_top_level_defs.py reads every module under src, scripts and tests and fails on a function or class name defined twice directly in a module body or in a class body (2,284 files, one hit: this); it was red before the rename and is green after. Ruff F811 did not report it because it ignores every name matching its default dummy-variable pattern, which is every name with a leading underscore (the same file with the underscore removed is reported); a call inside a function body does not count as a use for it.
